modules.topic_title: Punctuation - Full Stop, Question Mark, Speech Mark, Capital Letters
explanation_rules: Put a full stop at the end of a sentence that tells us something.
Put a question mark at the end of a sentence that asks something.
Put speech marks around the exact words someone says.
Start every sentence, name, and place with a capital letter.

questions.question_text: What punctuation mark is missing here? "Freya is playing in the forest__"
questions.explanation: This sentence tells us something, so it needs a full stop.

questions.question_text: What punctuation mark is missing here? "Can Oscar come to my party__"
questions.explanation: This sentence asks something, so it needs a question mark.

questions.question_text: Which word needs a capital letter? "sam can run very fast."
questions.explanation: Every sentence must start with a capital letter.

questions.question_text: Which words need speech marks around them? Harry asked, What time is it?
questions.explanation: Speech marks go around the exact words that Harry asked.

questions.question_text: What punctuation mark is missing here? "Zara ate some spaghetti__"
questions.explanation: This sentence tells us something, so it needs a full stop.

questions.question_text: This sentence used the wrong punctuation. Fix it: "Who is your best friend."
questions.explanation: This sentence asks something, so it needs a question mark, not a full stop.

questions.question_text: Fix the capital letters in this sentence: "finn is very kind."
questions.explanation: Names always start with a capital letter.

questions.question_text: Add speech marks to this sentence: Ivy asked, What time is it?
questions.explanation: Speech marks wrap around the words Ivy actually asked.

questions.question_text: Add the missing punctuation: "My puppy loves to play"
questions.explanation: A full stop is added because the sentence tells us something.

questions.question_text: This sentence used the wrong punctuation. Fix it: "When is your birthday."
questions.explanation: This sentence asks something, so it needs a question mark, not a full stop.

questions.question_text: Write a sentence about a place you know. Use a capital letter for its name.
questions.answer: Example: I would like to visit Oxford.
questions.explanation: Place names always start with a capital letter.

questions.question_text: Write a sentence where Ravi says "Watch out!" Use speech marks correctly.
questions.explanation: The spoken words sit inside speech marks, with a capital letter to start.

questions.question_text: Write a sentence about your family. Remember to use a full stop.
questions.answer: Example: My family went to the park.
questions.explanation: Any telling sentence that ends with a full stop is correct.

questions.question_text: Turn this into a question: "you like ice cream"
questions.explanation: Adding "Do" and a question mark turns this into a question.

questions.question_text: Write a sentence with your name in it. Remember the capital letter.
questions.explanation: Names always start with a capital letter.
